name: ActionsCounter
tagline: Project analytics on GitHub Actions alone — superseded by CFlair-Counter / ViewFlare.
summary: An event counter with no server: a single GitHub Actions workflow, run on demand from the Actions tab or by a repository_dispatch webhook, keeps per-project counts in the repository's own Actions variables as base64-encoded JSON, and a Vite dashboard published to GitHub Pages reads them back. A PostgreSQL storage mode is also implemented. This is the earlier approach to the problem; the current counter is CFlair-Counter (being renamed ViewFlare), which runs on Cloudflare Pages/Workers with D1 and serves counter.vkrishna04.me. ActionsCounter stays online as a working record of the Actions-based design.
highlights: No infrastructure at all — the counter is one workflow file, and the state lives in GitHub Actions repository variables rather than in any database you have to run.
Counts change only when the workflow is dispatched; there is no schedule, so a quiet project costs nothing.
A second storage mode swaps the Actions variables for a PostgreSQL table when the 48KB variable limit gets close.
Manual runs are gated on an admin password held as a repository secret, and webhook runs on a per-project token compared as a SHA-256 hash.
Superseded by CFlair-Counter / ViewFlare on Cloudflare Pages/Workers with D1 — kept as a record of the GitHub-Actions-only approach.

readme.heading: From the README
readme.markdown: # 🚀 ActionsCounter **Secure GitHub Actions-powered project analytics.** > **Superseded.** ActionsCounter is the earlier, GitHub-Actions-based counter; the current one is **CFlair-Counter** (being renamed **ViewFlare**), which runs on Cloudflare Pages/Workers with D1 and serves `counter.vkrishna04.me`. This repository stays up as a working record of the Actions-based approach. Track project usage, downloads, API calls, or any events. **How it actually works:** counts change only when the `Handle Projects` workflow runs, and that workflow runs only on demand — manually from the Actions tab (`workflow_dispatch`) or from a `repository_dispatch` webhook. There is no schedule and no cron; nothing updates on its own, and no push to this repository changes a count. **Where the data lives:** in the repository's own GitHub Actions variables — `PROJECTS_DATA` (base64-encoded JSON) and `ANALYTICS_DATA` — not in a file in this repository. Two other storage modes exist; see [Storage Modes](#-storage-modes). ## ⚡ Quick Start (5 Minutes) ### 1. Fork & Clone ```bash # Fork this repository on GitHub, then: git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/ActionsCounter.git cd ActionsCounter ``` ### 2. Generate Personal Access Token 📝 Create GitHub Token Required scopes: - ✅ `repo` - Full repository access - ✅ `workflow` - Update workflows and trigger actions - ✅ `admin:repo_hook` - Repository webhook access - ✅ `read:org` - Read organization data ### 3. Set Repository Secrets **[🔐 Configure Secrets](https://github.com/{YOUR_USERNAME}/ActionsCounter/settings/secrets/actions)** Replace `{YOUR_USERNAME}` with your GitHub username, then add: ``` ADMIN_PASSWORD = your_secure_password PAT_TOKEN = your_personal_access_token_from_step_2 ``` ### 4. Choose Storage Mode **[⚙️ Set Variables](https://github.com/{YOUR_USERNAME}/ActionsCounter/settings/variables/actions)** ``` STORAGE_MODE = 1 ``` **Storage Options:** - `1` = **GitHub Variables** (48KB, fast, recommended — and the fallback the workflow uses when `STORAGE_MODE` is unset) - `2` = **Database** (unlimited, requires PostgreSQL setup) - `3` = **Repository Commits** — **not implemented.** The workflow step is a stub that prints a warning and stores nothing. ### 5. Frontend Configuration Nothing to edit. `deploy-pages.yml` substitutes the owner and repository name into `frontend/src/main.ts` and `frontend/index.html` at build time. ### 6. Enable GitHub Pages **[📄 Setup GitHub Pages](https://github.com/{YOUR_USERNAME}/ActionsCounter/settings/pages)** Set source to: **GitHub Actions**. The dashboard is built and published by `deploy-pages.yml`, which runs on every push to `main` and on manual dispatch. ### 7. Test Your Setup **[🧪 Run Test Workflow](https://github.com/{YOUR_USERNAME}/ActionsCounter/actions/workflows/handle-projects.yml)** - Click "Run workflow" - Action: `list` - Password: your `ADMIN_PASSWORD` - Click "Run workflow" again ### 8. Access Your Dashboard **[🌐 View Dashboard](https://{YOUR_USERNAME}.github.io/ActionsCounter)** Replace `{YOUR_USERNAME}` with your actual GitHub username in all URLs above. ## 🎯 Usage ### Via GitHub Actions UI 1. **Actions** tab → **Handle Projects** 2. Choose action (`increment`, `add`, `list`, etc.) 3. Enter project name and password 4. Run workflow ### Via Webhook (`repository_dispatch`) ```bash curl -X POST \ -H "Authorization: token YOUR_PAT_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ https://api.github.com/repos/YOUR_USERNAME/ActionsCounter/dispatches \ -d '{ "event_type": "increment", "client_payload": { "project_alias": "proj_abc123", "auth_token": "the-projects-own-auth-token" } }' ``` ✅ **Secure**: no admin password in the request. The workflow SHA-256-hashes `auth_token` and compares it against the project's stored `auth_hash`; the admin password is read from repository secrets. > **Known limitation.** As committed, this webhook path does not complete. `project_alias` is read from the payload but never written to the step's outputs, so authentication always fails with "Project alias or auth token missing for webhook"; and the GitHub Variables operation step branches on `github.event.inputs.action`, which is empty for `repository_dispatch`. Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs are the path that works. ### Available Actions The Actions-tab form (`workflow_dispatch`) offers exactly these: - `increment` - Add 1 to project count - `decrement` - Subtract 1 from project count (floor 0) - `add` - Create new project - `remove` - Delete project - `set` - Change any field of a project, including its count and its name - `get` - View project details - `list` - Show all projects `repository_dispatch` also declares a `ping` event type, but no storage mode implements a `ping` branch. There is no `stats` action. ## 📊 Storage Modes | Mode | `STORAGE_MODE` | Where counts are stored | State | | ---- | -------------- | ----------------------- | ----- | | **GitHub Variables** | `1` (fallback default) | Actions repository variables `PROJECTS_DATA` and `ANALYTICS_DATA`, as base64-encoded JSON, bounded by GitHub's 48KB variable limit | Implemented | | **Database** | `2` | A PostgreSQL table, reached with `psql` from the runner | Implemented | | **Repository Commits** | `3` | — | **Stub.** The step prints "Repository commits mode operations need to be implemented" and stores nothing | `data/projects.json` in this repository is an empty seed file. No workflow reads or writes it — the live counts are in the `PROJECTS_DATA` Actions variable, so they live outside the git history entirely. **Recommended**: GitHub Variables (mode 1) — the default, and the only path that is routinely exercised. ## 🔒 Security Features - **Password Protection**: manual (`workflow_dispatch`) runs require the `ADMIN_PASSWORD` secret; webhook (`repository_dispatch`) runs authenticate against a per-project token instead, compared as a SHA-256 hash - **Repository Secrets**: Sensitive data stored securely in GitHub - **Token Validation**: GitHub token authentication - **No Browser Storage**: Zero sensitive data in localStorage ## 📚 Documentation - **[📖 Complete Documentation](./docs/Home.md)** - Comprehensive guides and references - **[🎯 Usage Examples](./docs/usage.md)** - Detailed usage examples and patterns - **[🔑 GitHub Token Scopes](./docs/token-scopes.md)** - Required Token permissions - **[⚡ Quick Setup](./docs/quick-setup.md)** - Detailed setup walkthrough - **[🔗 API Reference](./docs/api-reference.md)** - All actions and webhook examples - **[🗃️ Storage Modes](./docs/storage-overview.md)** - Choose the right storage mode ## 🛠️ Database Setup (Mode 2 Only) For Database mode, add these secrets: ``` DB_HOST = your_postgres_host DB_NAME = your_database_name DB_PORT = 5432 DB_USER = your_username DB_PASS = your_password DB_SCHEMA = myschema ``` **Free PostgreSQL Providers:** - [filess.io](https://filess.io) - 10MB free - [Supabase](https://supabase.com) - 500MB free - [Neon](https://neon.tech) - 512MB free ## 🌟 Example Use Cases - **Download Tracking**: Monitor software/file downloads - **API Analytics**: Track API endpoint usage - **Website Metrics**: Count page views and interactions - **Project Usage**: Monitor tool/library adoption - **Event Tracking**: Log application events ## 🔧 Support & Community ### 📚 **Documentation** - Found an issue? Let us know - **[✨ Request Feature](https://github.com/Life-Experimentalist/ActionsCounter/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml)** - Suggest new features - **[🆘 Support Guide](./docs/support.md)** - Comprehensive support information ### 🌟 **Contributing** - **[🤝 Contributing Guide](./docs/contributing.md)** - How to contribute to the project - **[👥 Contributors](https://github.com/Life-Experimentalist/ActionsCounter/graphs/contributors)** - Meet our amazing contributors **Quick Help:** - **"Invalid password" error:** Check `ADMIN_PASSWORD` secret is set correctly - **Analytics not showing:** `ANALYTICS_DATA` is seeded with zeros on first run, but the step that recomputes it is gated to the unimplemented repository-commits mode, so in GitHub Variables mode it never refreshes. Per-project counts still come from `PROJECTS_DATA`. - **Need immediate help?** Check our [FAQ](./docs/faq.md) first! ## 📄 License Apache 2.0 License - see [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md) --- **🚀 Ready to start tracking?** For a new setup, prefer **CFlair-Counter / ViewFlare**.
